B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate MCP fee was found. Vendor documentation says API access requires an API key and describes free and paid API plans; it does not explicitly state whether all MCP calls are free or how they map to API-plan charges.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: API plans: Free $0/month; Developer $49/month; Advanced $149/month; Pro $299/month; Business $599/month. A Portfolio package is separately priced from $999/month, with combined plan prices also listed.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The vendor lists monthly API credits, request-per-minute limits, endpoint access by plan, and separate Portfolio credits. Free: 25,000 credits and 60 RPM; paid tiers: 500,000–20,000,000 credits and 500–2,000 RPM. REST calls consume credits according to endpoint; requests exceeding limits return HTTP 429. MCP-specific billing is not specified.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Vendor docs say all endpoints require an API key. OAuth is required at the supplied MCP endpoint. Product API endpoint access and limits vary by subscription; whether these API plan restrictions apply identically to every MCP tool is not stated.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls OAuth and API service; the user selects or holds an API plan. Org-admin controls and client allowlists were not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official repository publishes annotations in its ChatGPT app submission metadata, including readOnlyHint, openWorldHint, and destructiveHint. The three build-* transaction tools are marked non-read-only and destructive; read tools are marked read-only. Runtime emission of these declarations is not independently confirmed. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow was documented. Companion skills ask the agent to confirm transaction intent and require the user to sign in their wallet; this is guidance, not verified server enforcement. 3. OAuth scopes are openid, email, mcp:read, mcp:write. API docs require an API key. Product permission inheritance, token lifetime/revocation, org admin controls, and client allowlists: Unknown. 4. No read-only endpoint, filters, toolsets, query-free mode, or environment/region variants were found for the supplied host. Vendor docs describe API endpoint/plan access limits. 5. Public app-submission metadata says transaction builders do not accept private keys and return unsigned transactions; skills also warn against asking for seed phrases. Other PII masking and data boundaries: Unknown. 6. API plans publish credit and RPM limits; MCP-specific caps and result truncation: Unknown. 7. Runtime argument validation, coercion, and overrides: Unknown; hosted runtime code is not public. 8. MCP audit logging and telemetry: Unknown. Vendor pricing docs say the API dashboard provides usage stats/history. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, or report tool appears in the 44-tool inventory. `get-x402-access-guide` provides pay-per-call guidance but does not itself send payment. 10. Three skills are distributed separately in the public repository; examples include tool selection, confirmation and signing guidance. These are not shown as server-enforced rules. 11. No persistent MCP memory or behavior-dependent tool exposure documented. 12. The current input endpoint is documented as a flat set of 44 endpoint-specific tools. A separate legacy/docs-host endpoint exists. 13. No raw arbitrary HTTP request, SQL, shell, or script tool appears in the current inventory. The older endpoint's `execute-request` is not part of the current input endpoint inventory.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The companion skills recommend confirming intent before building transactions, having users sign in their own wallet, using small limits, and avoiding private keys/seed phrases. These are client/plugin instructions; the hosted runtime source is unavailable, so enforcement is unverified. The product guide recommends using Claude.ai rather than Claude Desktop via mcp-remote for live API execution.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The public app-submission metadata states: “It does not take private keys, and it does not broadcast transactions for you.” The repository says transaction-building tools return an unsigned transaction for the user to review and sign in their own wallet. Privacy policy and terms URLs are advertised in OAuth metadata, but their relevant policy text was not retrievable in the prepared evidence or browser review.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor describes the server as providing live Solana API access, schema discovery, and code generation grounded in the API specification. The repository describes OAuth connection and says not to commit API keys.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The returned-unsigned-transaction behavior and transaction-builder annotations are present in public submission metadata, but runtime implementation is not public. User confirmation and private-key avoidance appear as companion-skill guidance; server enforcement is not established. Privacy, retention, and training promises could not be compared because policy text was unavailable.

contradictions: The official product guide and its changelog describe four tools: list-endpoints, search-endpoints, get-endpoint, and execute-request. The current official repository inventory for the same hosted product lists 44 endpoint-specific tools instead. VerifyMCP recorded the 44-tool inventory on 2026-10-27; ProtocolProbe had observed 7 older tools on 2026-10-08. This indicates tool-set changes or endpoint/version drift; the vendor guide does not yet match the current repository inventory.

The product guide says Claude Desktop via mcp-remote exposes only 3 of 4 tools, whereas the current repository documents a different 44-tool inventory. This compatibility statement applies to the older documented set and does not establish the availability of each current tool in that client.

OAuth metadata supports both mcp:read and mcp:write scopes, while the current official inventory consists mostly of read tools plus three unsigned transaction builders. The scope metadata does not explain per-tool permission mapping.

Older MCP Registry entries identify https://docs.vybenetwork.com/mcp as a separate server with schema discovery and live API execution; the supplied endpoint is https://mcp.vybenetwork.xyz/mcp and has a distinct OAuth-protected resource. Their tool inventories should not be combined.
observations_for_research: The current repository names separate tools for endpoint-specific API operations, while the older product guide described generic API-schema discovery and request execution tools.
The public repository distributes behavioral skills separately from the MCP endpoint, including workflow instructions and guidance to confirm transaction intent.

The three build-* tools produce unsigned transaction payloads, with official submission annotations marking them destructive despite documentation stating they are not signed or broadcast by the server.
OAuth grants broad mcp:read and mcp:write scopes; the published metadata does not map those scopes to specific tools or Vybe API plan entitlements.
notes: Reviewed prepared links.json, pages/ (including official page text, HTML, and script extracts), links_check.txt, and the local official repository at aff7c7264bd72b9262319fa14f28f33ae4115644. The repository is official and tied to the hosted endpoint, but it is configuration, submission metadata, and skills rather than runtime code. No repo-wide license file, runtime language/SDK, tool input schemas for the current 44-tool set, initialize instructions, tool result envelopes, token expiry/revocation, MCP-specific price, or public governance policy text was found. Official docs-search/API MCP endpoint at docs.vybenetwork.com is distinct from the input endpoint. Unofficial community servers were not used as evidence.
